root_motivation: The 2026-09-17 15:54:42Z proof-lane gate went red on reviewer-agent:infra even though the reviewer had returned a valid block verdict; a finalize rejection needs to carry the rejected verdict so a real finding is never hidden behind a generic infra label.
user_persona: The build loop's gate on RedBaron and the operator reading its GATES line.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given extend-gate.sh's own verification step, When the branch's gate runs, Then the verification output is present and named in the receipt.

five_whys_trace: why did the gate go red on reviewer-agent:infra? because finalize rejected the reviewer's receipt.
why did finalize reject it? because intent_card_sha was bare hex, not sha256:-prefixed.
why did the reviewer write bare hex? the prompt only said "the sha256 of intent-card.json", not which exact string to copy.
why was there no exact string to copy? review-request.json named the field intent_card_sha256, the receipt schema names it intent_card_sha — no shared name to copy verbatim.
why did nobody catch this sooner? nine of ten prior runs happened to include the prefix by convention, not by contract.
